A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, research questions, and core experiments. The main text, figures, equations, references, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments measuring execution horizons, injected-error effects, model scaling, and mitigation strategies on synthetic tasks.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and additionally reports matrix-multiplication results and the authors' analysis of annotated failures from agent benchmarks.

M1.justification: The core framework still supplies the plan and dictionary, evaluates retrieve-then-compose execution, and measures execution horizons. Existing self-verification, context-window, and majority-voting procedures are retained. Matrix multiplication extends task coverage within this framework; it does not introduce a new model or solution algorithm.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained dictionary-addition and component tasks, v3 adds chained 2-by-2 matrix multiplication in Appendix B. Appendix A adds manual analysis of AgentErrorBench failure trajectories from GAIA, ALFWorld, and WebShop. This substantially broadens operations and application domains, although the latter analysis does not involve new end-to-end agent runs.

E2.justification: Figure 7 adds reported comparisons for Qwen3-235B-A22B and Qwen3-Next, which were absent from v1's corresponding plot despite the earlier setup mentioning a 235B Qwen model. The new matrix comparison also includes Kimi-K2-Thinking. The original benchmark's existing model lineup is retained.

E3.justification: The original binary-search benchmark retains its 80% success criterion, stated rollout allocations, and decoding settings. Added evaluations introduce manual screening of failure annotations and matrix tests using 50 independent test rollouts per model with entries in [-9,9]. These are additional protocols, not documented changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds realistic-agent failure cases and categorization, and tests the original single-turn task's parallelizability limitation through matrix multiplication. Figure 17 supplies accuracy and format-failure curves for programmatically generated CoT histories, whereas v1 only described attempted experiments and their confounders. Earlier mitigation, temperature, complexity, and component ablations remain.

E5.justification: Figure 4 newly displays and identifies bands as mean plus or minus one standard deviation over 100 samples. v1 described moving averages there, although other figures already contained error bars. The 100-rollout allocation was already documented in v1, so this does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Figure 7 changes GPT-5's reported horizon from 1024 to 2176 under the retained stated criterion and adds Qwen results of 80 and 352. DeepSeek-R1 remains at 120 in both plots; v3 corrects the introduction's earlier claim of 200. New matrix and CoT results are reported, alongside estimated self-conditioning-like patterns in roughly 20%, 48%, and 33% of analyzed GAIA, ALFWorld, and WebShop failures.

T1.justification: The horizon formula, proof, and sensitivity derivation are retained. Independence, already used in v1's proof, becomes explicit in the proposition. Section 2.1 replaces the faster-than-exponential characterization with hyperbolic growth, and Appendix B adds a complexity-theoretic argument contrasting addition with iterated matrix multiplication through the cited TC0/TC1 distinction.

C1.justification: The central contributions concerning execution, scaling, and self-conditioning remain. The abstract qualifies small-model single-turn accuracy from 100% to near-perfect and changes thinking models' elimination of self-conditioning to mitigation, although the body retains stronger 'fixes' language. These are limited qualifications rather than a redefinition of the paper's contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive discussion of the single-turn task's parallelizability and limited future applicability, multiple valid plans, and subjectivity in identifying self-conditioning in realistic trajectories. It also links self-conditioning to in-context learning and interprets Qwen3-Next's results as suggesting an architectural influence. These extend the original mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v3 provides the matrix task's full prompt, value range, identity initialization, and output format, plus a source link for the analyzed failure trajectories. A new reproducibility statement says source code, generation scripts, and exact datapoints accompany the supplement. Existing code/data links, hardware, token limits, and decoding parameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands substantially through connections to exposure bias, RL-based self-correction, self-refinement, in-context learning, and snowballing hallucinations. New agent-benchmark and circuit-complexity references support the added analyses. The earlier tau-bench reliability discussion and standalone controlled-synthetic-evaluation discussion are removed or recast; this exceeds bibliographic updating.

P1.justification: The formulation is reorganized around an earlier motivating example and explicit terminology before the mathematical analysis. Substantial prose is rewritten, discussion material moves into related work, and the Discussion becomes a Conclusion with a separate reproducibility statement. These changes restructure the narrative beyond accommodating new experiments.

P2.justification: Several central displays are redesigned: Figure 2 replaces the exponential comparison with multiple success thresholds; Figure 4 adds a first-step panel, uncertainty bands, and a hypothetical reference; Figure 7 adopts a logarithmic horizon axis. New matrix and CoT figures, revised summary graphics, boxed definitions, and relocated appendix figures substantially change presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision through the hyperbolic-growth explanation, corrected result statements, clearer definitions, and explicit uncertainty reporting. The matrix experiment directly addresses a previously unexamined limitation of the single-turn benchmark. However, the added realistic-agent estimates remain subjective and the CoT analysis retains acknowledged confounders, limiting the strength of the additional validation. The net gain is useful but bounded.
